sources.title: The 100-Year Life: Living and Working in an Age of Longevity
sources.publisher: Lynda Gratton and Andrew J. Scott, Bloomsbury (2016)
supports: FT Business Book of the Year shortlist
sources.limits: Popular trade nonfiction, not peer-reviewed empirical research; a projection/heuristic rather than a guaranteed demographic outcome, noted explicitly in the chapter.

sources.title: The New Map of Life initiative
sources.publisher: Stanford Center on Longevity (Laura Carstensen, founding director)
sources.limits: Advocacy/policy-research initiative whose explicit mission is to promote longer, engaged lives — its normative framing is noted as such in the chapter.

sources.title: Socioemotional selectivity theory
sources.publisher: Laura L. Carstensen, multiple peer-reviewed publications from the 1990s onward
supports: perceived time horizon, not chronological age, drives prioritization of emotionally meaningful goals
sources.limits: Well-established in social/developmental psychology; extending it to financial or family-formation decision-making specifically remains a thinner, less settled body of evidence, noted explicitly in the chapter.
